analyst_view.overall: Early view: Cádiz are 20th and on their third coach of the season, Borja Jiménez, who took over in late October; they won his debut against Ceuta but then lost 2-1 at Mallorca and 2-1 at home to Oviedo despite creating more. Córdoba are tenth under Iván Ania after a 3-0 win over Ceuta, though one preview listed five injured players. This Andalusian meeting carries real pressure for Cádiz, who have only two home wins.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals. Córdoba's games are open (22 scored and 22 conceded, and their away games average over three goals), while Cádiz's home games have averaged just over two; the two pull in different directions, so I stay near the site's number.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.9 corners. That looks right: Córdoba won 11 corners against Ceuta and attack wide, and Cádiz under Borja Jiménez pushed hard enough against Oviedo to win six, so both sides should contribute.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.9 cards. I lean higher: Cádiz-Oviedo produced nine yellows, Córdoba had Isma Ruiz sent off for two yellows and Alex banned for violent play after their trip to Celta Fortuna, and a regional game with Cádiz fighting relegation should be tense.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.1 shots. Cádiz took 15 against Oviedo and Córdoba 14 against Ceuta, and both teams commit players forward, so a total close to the site's number fits.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. I lean slightly lower: Cádiz got only four of their 15 shots on target against Oviedo, with six blocked, and their finishing has been the main problem all season.
